The smartphone has become the most ubiquitous camera in history. Its ubiquity means most people have never taken a proper photography course. In this article, we'll offer some basic photography concepts so you can use your phone to its fullest capabilities. Here are five ideas that will help you get better photos with your phone.

1. Always Have a Subject
If you've ever tried to capture a moment of nature with your phone you've probably noticed that your subject changes if the sun moves in the frame. If your subject is the beach at sunset, you need to pay attention to the movement of the sun so it doesn't sneak into your photo. Always keep a subject, otherwise your photos will lack a focal point. It may also be a good idea to choose an interesting subject.

2. Know the Right Moments
Some photos will be taken in a matter of minutes. They will be planned well in advance and won't leave you with time to spare. It's not just in photography that these kinds of photos are better, but in film as well. A film that has a lot of time in between shots to edit is a film that takes more effort than it needs to. 

3. Try New Subjects
Your phone is very versatile in its ability to capture multiple types of subjects. It can take many different shots and it is very easy to make your own version of a particular shot. Your phone can also capture many more subjects than your DSLR can, so if you've always dreamed of capturing a great photograph of a specific subject you've never had the opportunity to capture, your phone will give you that opportunity.

4. Learn to Use Lighting
Lighting will affect the quality of a photograph. When using a flash or a strong light source it is important to remember that the light will reflect back from the subject. Light reflecting off of a person will give your photo a very bright appearance. If you use a light source that reflects the light off the subject, you may get a bright and bold image, but the photo will not show the subject the same way that a regular light will. 

5. Understand Shutter Speed
You can control how long the shutter stays open. You can set it to 1/50th of a second, which will produce an image with a great deal of motion blur. You can set it to 1/1000th of a second, which will capture movement and give the subject of your photo a much clearer appearance.<|end_of_text|>
